title: Edward Clem, Tig Chambers, Manuel Manetta and Clayborne Williams
summary: Questions about various musicians: Edward Clem of St. James, Tig Chambers, a two-horn teacher, and the Clayborne Williams family of Donaldsonville who played Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: What about Edward Clem, did you ever know him, Edward Clem?
Yeah, well he done that, yeah, he played good something. But he don't play that uh, that thing, he can't play that somehow or another. He played more so that uh, bop music.
Edward Clem?
No, Edward, oh, Edward Clem, he's dead. He used to live in St. Jean.
Yeah, that's a problem.

Yeah, that's a problem. I thought you were talking about uh, boy living in the city there, Brownsley Lune, how you call him? No. He talking about the high-five, boy? He just heard Marshall from Cross River. Oh, he talking about Dave? Yeah, Dave, I thought you were talking about Dave.
He's from across the river?
Yeah, Dave, I'm sorry, he come from across the river. But Marshall didn't want to show him how the place. He didn't know nothing. When he left here, he didn't know nothing.
Where's Dave from? What town?
From Cross River, somewhere across the river.
Well, what about Edward Clem? He's from up around St. James?
St. James, about St. James, that's right.
And what kind of music did he play?
He played trumpet.
Did he play Dixieland or?
Yeah, he played Dixieland too. He was all, all, all the fellas I think could play Dixieland.
Did you ever hear Buddy Bowlin?
No, I don't know, I don't know Buddy. That's what he used to play there too. All of them used to play Dixieland music.
Very few people remember him.
I know. Did you know him? No, I didn't kind of hear his name. I didn't ever see him. No, I never seen him.
What about Tig Chambers? Did you know him? No, I don't know him. You must have known him, huh? Yeah, I know.
I know Chambers.
Who did he work with anyway? I know.
He had his own outfit I think. He fell across, what you call him? Thomas, what? Teach Thomas. He played two horns. He can play two horns on him.
Oh, that's Professor Moneta.
Yeah, he played two horns. He played sax, he played anything. Piano, he gave a lesson. Oh yeah, he used to, he used to do that. We used to call him horse. Yeah. He used to stomp so much.
He'd stomp his feet?

Yeah, he'd stand up and talk to him. He'd listen to four of them. Yeah, they'd want that to hold. Yeah, they'd want that to hold. You don't have to make your music good, you know. First, that's all his playing, all that that. I said, what about him first come from? He ain't got no movement. I never did see Buddy Bowler. That's the fault I sure didn't want to see. Never did see. Bump, I saw Bump. Oh, you jumped. That's what you wanted. I was born from Plackmont. I think so, yeah. Yeah, Plackmont. Yeah, Plackmont. Well, they had some good musicians out there. They were St. Gene, they had some good ones. But they left there and went to Baton Rouge.
Who was that from St. James?
That was, uh, Clackmont. Called his name a while ago.
Is that from Donaldsonville?

That's from Donaldsonville, yeah. Old man, uh, Clayborne Williams. Yeah, that'd be Clayborne Williams. He died when his son still played. He played in Baton Rouge. But he still played Dixieland music. Clayborne? Yeah, old man Clayborne's been there.
His son plays Dixieland?

Oh yeah, he's good, good. Yeah, yeah, George. He's doing anything. When he first started playing, he was a little boy with Harvard. Uncle Luke, super big as that. Used to play that with his dad. I remember that girl.
It's the tiny boy, huh?

Yeah, his sister's playing piano. He's pretty good. He used to stop here all the time. He stopped here about 17 years. He used to play back every labor day. He played back here. And from here, they go to town and play. Go in.
